requirement:
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. It MUST derive the node's
inclusive line range, including attached comments and attributes, during
validation for display and reference coverage. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, unsupported language, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
rationale:
**Verdict: the requirement is satisfied.** I read the marked `{impl}` and `{test}` code. I did not open the outline, parsing or hashing code itself, because that belongs to the cited outline, selector and structural-hash requirements.

**Implementation**
- `OutlineCache::parse` (src/inputs.rs:69-96) reads the file through the containment check. It parses it with the profile chosen by file extension (`outline::parse`, `profile_for_path`) and caches the result.
- Missing, unreadable or disallowed files yield "cannot open/read …" or containment errors. Parse failures yield `"{file}: cannot parse {profile} source"`.
- `ParsedSource::resolve` (src/inputs.rs:100-120) resolves `item` to exactly one node. It reports invalid selectors, ambiguous selectors ("add a #N disambiguator") and selectors that match nothing, each with a distinct message.
- `InputSelector::resolve` (src/inputs.rs:239-326) returns the node's structural hash, its kind and its current inclusive line range via `node_range`. The range is derived at validation time from the outline node, and per the outlines requirement that node includes its attached comments and attributes.
- `validate_outline_input` (src/evidence.rs:749-810) checks the key set `{file, item, hash}` and that the hash is a 64-character lowercase hex digest. It resolves the selector and compares `node.hash` with the recorded hash. A mismatch reports "outline input changed: file item (now lines a-b) no longer has the recorded hash". This is a structural comparison, so moving nodes, editing other nodes and editing unhashed comments do not invalidate an input.
- Supporting code is marked correctly: `outline_input` and `outline_inputs_for_lines` build inputs. `to_input` records only the selector and hash, with no line numbers or text. `index.rs` renders the inputs and flags stale hashes.
- The "unsupported language" obligation is met by the plain-text fallback profile. Every text file has a profile, so the only failure left is an unreadable (for example non-UTF-8) file, which is reported as "cannot read".

**Tests**
- `outline_inputs_survive_moves_and_unhashed_comments_but_not_edits` (tests/evidence_boundaries.rs:50) covers most of the design space:
  - Inputs stay valid after nodes or lines move, code is reflowed, and unhashed comments are edited.
  - Editing code or a doc comment makes the input stale, and the error names the file, selector and current line range.
  - An edited plain-text line produces "no outline node matches".
  - It also covers a missing node, an ambiguous selector, an invalid selector, a bad hash format, a missing file, a parse failure (`src/broken.rs`), and unexpected fields.
- `collects_missing_orphan_format_false_and_changed_line_errors` (src/evidence.rs:1507) covers the changed-hash message and the missing-node, empty-file and bad-hash errors.
- The symlink, external-path and Cargo-output tests cover the containment, freshness and disallow interplay with outline inputs.
- `line_range_reads_record_the_innermost_covering_nodes` (src/authoring/tools.rs:1490) covers the line-range-to-outline-node mapping and that recorded inputs omit line numbers and text.
- `tests/outcomes.rs` covers stale-input reporting through the status output.
- `selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor` covers selector resolution against anchors.

**Gaps:** none found. No FIXMEs are needed. Attributes and doc comments are covered by the shared outline profile, and the tests exercise the line ranges (`fn[beta]` lines 4-6 include its doc and line comments).

text: :::{req} outline_inputs
For an outline input, Habeas MUST parse `file` with its language's grammar under
{cite}`requirements.references.outlines` and resolve `item` to exactly one
outline node under {cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. It MUST
compare `hash` with the node's current structural hash under
{cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. It MUST derive the node's
inclusive line range, including attached comments and attributes, during
validation for display and reference coverage. Moving the node, editing other
nodes, or editing comments its profile does not hash MUST NOT invalidate the
input. Habeas MUST report a missing file, unsupported language, parse failure,
invalid or ambiguous selector, or changed hash.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline; other
nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline descendants appear under the
nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure: the kinds of its named grammar nodes and the text
of its leaf tokens, in source order, including siblings its profile attaches to
it. It MUST exclude whitespace and comments, except comment kinds its profile
includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. Prose, namely Markdown
text and the text of hashed comments, MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words,
where words are separated by whitespace and the whitespace itself, including
leading and trailing whitespace, is never hashed. Each word MUST be encoded
separately, so `ab cd` and `abcd` differ. Comment delimiters, such as `//`, `///`, `//!`,
`/*`, `*/`, and a leading `*` on a continuation line, MUST NOT be part of a
hashed comment's text, so reflowing a comment run across more or fewer lines
does not change the hash; code
string literals MUST be hashed as written. A `line` node's hash MUST be the
digest of the line's text without leading and trailing whitespace. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
